# TsugaCollector

**API:** `observability.tsuga.com/v1alpha1` · **Scope:** Namespaced · **Short name:** `tscol`

Run a custom OpenTelemetry collector from a native `OpenTelemetryCollector` spec, rendered as `tsuga-<name>`. The toggles add export to the node agent, self-telemetry and default processors without replacing anything the spec defines. Requires TsugaCollectorConfig named `cluster`. Resource names are limited to 36 characters. See the [custom collectors guide](../kubernetes-monitoring/custom-collectors.md).

## Fields

Required is relative to the containing object. Defaults inside optional objects apply only when the containing object exists. Status is read-only. Standard Kubernetes metadata fields are omitted.

| Field | Type | Required | Schema default | Description and constraints |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spec` | object | No | — | TsugaCollectorSpec wraps a native OpenTelemetryCollector spec. The operator renders it as OpenTelemetryCollector tsuga-<name>, adding only what the toggles enable. Nothing the spec already defines is replaced.  |
| `spec.collector` | object | Yes | — | OpenTelemetryCollector spec (opentelemetry.io/v1beta1), passed through. The operator adds only what the toggles enable, and fills image, resources and security contexts when unset. Creating a TsugaCollector is equivalent to creating pods in its namespace, with access to every Secret and ServiceAccount there; grant it like pod create. Opaque JSON; validated by Tsuga |
| `spec.defaultProcessors` | boolean | No | `true` | Puts memory_limiter first and batch last in every pipeline that does not pass its data to a forward, routing, failover, round_robin or datadog connector and has none of that type yet.  |
| `spec.selfTelemetry` | boolean | No | `true` | Sends the collector's internal metrics to the node agent, unless service.telemetry.metrics is already set.  |
| `spec.tsugaExporter` | boolean | No | `true` | Adds an otlp/tsuga-agent exporter, which sends to the node agent, to every pipeline that does not pass its data to a forward, routing, failover, round_robin or datadog connector. The agent adds the Tsuga credentials and cluster enrichment.  |

| `status.conditions` | array of object | No | — | Conditions carries the standard Kubernetes condition set. Both collection controllers publish a single "Ready" condition whose reason names the reconcile stage that failed.  |
| `status.conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string | Yes | — | lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.  |
| `status.conditions[].message` | string | Yes | — | message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. maxLength: `32768` |
| `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer | No | — | observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. minimum: `0` |
| `status.conditions[].reason` | string | Yes | — | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. This field may not be empty. minLength: `1`; maxLength: `1024`; pattern: `"^[A-Za-z]([A-Za-z0-9_,:]*[A-Za-z0-9_])?$"` |
